subtitle: How well do you really know your people?
author: Dennis Nickens, AKA Spiritual Romeo

cards.text: When [Subject]'s friend is going through something hard, [Subject] usually:

options.text: Drops everything and shows up in person
Sends a thoughtful text and follows up later
Waits to be asked because they don't want to overstep
Means well but forgets to follow through

cards.playNotes: Other players each pick a letter. Reveal at the same time. Subject reveals which is true. Scoring: 2 points for the correct letter. Subject gets 1 point for every correct guess.

cards.text: If you texted [Subject] at 2 a.m. saying "are you up?" they would:

options.text: Call you within five minutes
Reply with a text but not call
See it in the morning and check in then
Probably miss it entirely until you mentioned it

cards.playNotes: Reveal at the same time. Subject reveals truth. Scoring: 2 points correct + 1 point to Subject per correct guesser.

cards.text: [Subject]'s last canceled plan was canceled because:

options.text: They were genuinely sick or had an emergency
Work blew up at the last minute
Their energy was low and they couldn't fake it
Something better came along
They forgot until it was too late
Family pulled them away

cards.playNotes: Reveal at the same time. Subject reveals truth. Scoring: 3 points correct + 1 point to Subject per correct guesser.

cards.text: The version of [Subject] their friends get at parties versus the version they get one on one is:

options.text: Identical, [Subject] is the same everywhere
Different but only slightly
Noticeably different, [Subject] performs more in groups
Two totally different people

cards.text: [Subject] has flaked on a friend in the past month.
cards.playNotes: Players write T or F. Reveal at the same time. Subject reveals truth. Scoring: 1 point correct + 1 point to Subject per correct guesser.

cards.text: When [Subject] says "let me know if you need anything," they:

options.text: Mean it and will show up if asked
Mean it but secretly hope they don't get asked
Say it out of habit without thinking
Are already planning to follow up before you ask

cards.text: Point to the person in this room you think [Subject] would call FIRST if they got terrible news right now.
cards.playNotes: All players point at the same time. Subject reveals who they would actually call. If the person Subject would call is sitting at the table, players who pointed at them score. If Subject would call someone NOT at the table, no one scores on the point but Subject reveals who. Scoring: 2 points for correctly pointing. 3 points to Subject if a majority pointed correctly.

cards.text: The friend [Subject] is the BEST at showing up for is best described as:

options.text: The one who's been going through it for years
The one [Subject] has known the longest
The newest friend [Subject] is still impressing
The one who makes it easy by asking directly
The one [Subject] feels guilty about because they show up so much
[Subject] would say they show up equally for everyone

cards.text: [Subject], tell us about a moment recently when you wished you had shown up for someone and didn't. What got in the way?
cards.playNotes: Subject shares. Others listen. No guessing, no scoring.

cards.text: Group discussion: What's the difference between being a present friend and being a busy friend? Is there a line, and who decides where it is?
cards.playNotes: Everyone weighs in. No scoring. Move on when the conversation runs its course.

cards.text: When [Subject] is at dinner with a friend, their phone is:

options.text: Face down on the table, untouched
In their pocket on silent
On the table face up so they can glance
In their hand at least once per course

cards.text: The last friend [Subject] reached out to first (no reply chain, no obligation) was:

options.text: Someone in this room
A friend they see less than once a month
A friend who lives in a different city
Honestly, they cannot remember

cards.text: The hardest truth [Subject] is currently NOT telling a friend is most likely about:

options.text: How they actually feel about that friend
Something the friend is doing that's not working
Something [Subject] is going through privately
Something [Subject] regrets from their shared past

cards.text: When a friend asks [Subject] "what do you really think," [Subject] usually:

options.text: Tells them straight, no softening
Tells them but cushions it
Asks what they want to hear and steers there
Avoids the question by reframing it

cards.text: [Subject] tells the most lies (even small ones) to friends about:

options.text: How they really feel about other friends in the group
Why they canceled a plan
How well they're actually doing
How they spent their weekend
Their feelings about another friend's partner
[Subject] would say they don't lie to friends

cards.text: [Subject] has lied to someone in this room in the past month.
cards.playNotes: Reveal at the same time. Subject reveals. Scoring: 1 + 1.

cards.text: The thing [Subject] hides from their friends to seem "fine" is mostly:

options.text: Financial stress
Loneliness even in a full room
How much they actually need their friends
That something they do for fun is actually exhausting

cards.text: If a friend asked [Subject] "do you actually like spending time with me," [Subject] would:

options.text: Say yes immediately and mean it
Say yes and partly mean it
Pause too long before answering
Honestly ask "why are you asking that"

cards.text: Point to the person in this room you think [Subject] is most honest with about themselves.
cards.playNotes: All players point at the same time. Subject reveals who they're actually most honest with (in or out of the room). Scoring: 2 for pointing correctly. 3 to Subject if a majority pointed at the person Subject named.

cards.text: The truth [Subject] most wishes one specific friend would just SAY to them is:

options.text: "I miss you and I'm not great at saying it"
"I'm jealous of how your life looks right now"
"You changed and I'm not sure how to be your friend now"
"I need more from you than I'm asking for"
"I'm proud of you and I never say it enough"
"I'm struggling and I don't know how to bring it up"

cards.text: When [Subject] disagrees with what a friend is doing, [Subject] usually:

options.text: Says it directly the next time it comes up
Talks about it with a different friend first
Sits with it and hopes the friend figures it out
Says nothing because it's not their place

cards.text: [Subject], tell us one truth about yourself that you have rehearsed telling a friend but never have. Don't tell us who, just what.
Group discussion: Is there such a thing as too honest with a friend? When does honesty become an excuse for cruelty?
The friend [Subject] is currently NOT telling something important to is most likely:

options.text: Someone in this room
A friend they've known the longest
A friend they don't see often anymore
The friend who'd take it the hardest

cards.text: In the last 30 days, [Subject] has done something significant for a friend that cost them:

options.text: Real money
A full day or evening
A hard conversation they didn't want to have
Nothing significant, honestly

cards.text: [Subject]'s friendships function more like:

options.text: A bank account where they always make deposits
A bank account where they always take withdrawals
Roughly balanced
[Subject] honestly has no idea

cards.text: The friend [Subject] is currently UNDER-investing in is:

options.text: The one they've known the longest
The newest friend they made
A friend they had a small fight with
A friend who's been needier than usual
A friend doing too well and [Subject] feels unneeded
Someone in this room

cards.text: [Subject] reached out to a friend first (no prompt, no obligation) within the last week.
Last time a friend hit a real milestone (engagement, promotion, hard recovery, real win), [Subject]:

options.text: Called or showed up immediately
Sent a thoughtful text or gift
Liked the post and meant to follow up
Did not see it / did not act

cards.text: The most recent thing [Subject] did just because a friend would enjoy it:

options.text: Within the last week
Within the last month
Within the last six months
Honestly cannot remember

cards.text: Point to the person in this room you think [Subject] has invested the MOST time in over the past year.
cards.playNotes: Pointing at the same time. Scoring: 2 for pointing correctly. 3 to Subject if half or more pointed correctly.

cards.text: The cost of [Subject]'s friendships shows up most as:

options.text: Time
Money
Emotional weight they carry quietly
Sleep, schedule, their own peace
Career or family time they trade for friend time
Friendships do not currently cost [Subject] much

cards.text: When a friend asks [Subject] for a favor, [Subject] usually:

options.text: Says yes before thinking about whether they can
Says yes and resents it later
Pauses and gives an honest yes or no
Defers the answer and forgets to come back

cards.text: The friend [Subject] could do something thoughtful for THIS WEEK, that they probably won't, is:

options.text: Someone in this room
The friend going through the hardest thing right now
A long-distance friend they keep losing touch with
A friend who reached out and didn't get a real reply
A friend they owe an apology to
[Subject] is honestly planning to do something for someone already

cards.text: Group discussion: What does it actually cost to be a great friend? Is it possible to be one without trading something away?
[Subject]'s friendships would suffer the most if [Subject] suddenly:

options.text: Lost the ability to text quickly
Could not spend money on friends for a year
Could not see anyone in person for six months
Stopped initiating contact entirely

cards.text: [Subject] knows their best friend's:

options.text: Greatest fear right now
Greatest hope for the next year
Both
Neither, honestly

cards.text: The thing [Subject] does NOT know about a close friend, that they probably should, is:

options.text: What their parents are actually like
The exact moment something hard happened to them
What their relationship with money is
What their faith situation actually is

cards.text: The friend [Subject] knows the LEAST about (despite calling them close) is:

options.text: The friend with the loudest personality
The friend who always asks about [Subject] but deflects from themselves
The friend [Subject] has known the longest (and assumes they know already)
The newest friend who hasn't opened up yet
A friend in this room
[Subject] would say they know all their close friends deeply

cards.text: [Subject] could name the three biggest things happening in their best friend's life right now.
cards.playNotes: Reveal. Subject reveals truth (and offers to name them if they can). Scoring: 1 + 1.

cards.text: Of all the people in this room, [Subject] knows most about:

options.text: Person to Subject's left
Person across the table
Person to Subject's right
Honestly, knows everyone in the room about equally

cards.playNotes: Subject's neighbors can choose who fits A/B/C from where they sit. Reveal. Subject reveals. Scoring: 2 + 1.

cards.text: The last thing [Subject] learned about a friend that genuinely surprised them was about:

options.text: Their childhood
A current struggle
Their finances or work
Their faith or beliefs

cards.text: Point to the person in this room you think KNOWS [Subject] the best.
cards.playNotes: All point at the same time. Subject reveals who they think knows them best. Scoring: 2 for pointing at the person Subject named. 3 to Subject if a majority pointed at the same person Subject did.

cards.text: The biggest gap in [Subject]'s knowledge about a close friend is:

options.text: What their childhood was actually like
What they're afraid of right now
What they want out of the next five years
What they think of [Subject]
What their relationship with God or faith is
Something else entirely

cards.text: [Subject] could tell you their best friend's deepest fear:

options.text: Word for word, [Subject] knows it cold
Roughly, [Subject] has a sense
[Subject] could guess but isn't sure
[Subject] honestly does not know

cards.text: [Subject], name a friend who knows something about you that almost no one else knows. Without revealing the secret, tell us why that friend earned that level of trust.
When [Subject] thinks of their three closest friends, the one [Subject] would have the HARDEST time describing accurately to a stranger is:

options.text: The funniest one
The most successful one
The one [Subject] sees most often
The one [Subject] has known the longest

cards.text: If [Subject] had to write a one-sentence description of each close friend, the friend they'd struggle most to capture is:

options.text: The most complicated one
The one [Subject] is closest to
The newest one
The one [Subject] sees only occasionally
The one [Subject] doesn't fully understand
[Subject] could describe all of them easily

cards.text: The last time [Subject] hurt a friend, [Subject] handled it by:

options.text: Saying sorry quickly and meaning it
Apologizing but explaining why it happened
Hoping it would blow over
Not realizing they'd hurt the friend at all

cards.text: [Subject]'s apologies tend to be:

options.text: Specific, direct, no excuses
Heartfelt but with a defense built in
Quick and slightly awkward
Rare, [Subject] does not apologize easily

cards.text: The friend [Subject] currently owes the biggest apology to is:

options.text: Someone in this room
A friend [Subject] hasn't talked to in months
A friend [Subject] talks to every day
A friend who already moved on without it
A friend who is still waiting for it
[Subject] doesn't believe they owe anyone an apology right now

cards.text: There is a friendship [Subject] has lost in the past five years that they secretly believe could have been saved if [Subject] had handled the repair differently.
A friend has apologized to [Subject] in the past year and [Subject] has not fully accepted it.
When [Subject] is the one who needs to apologize, [Subject]'s first instinct is to:

options.text: Move toward the conversation immediately
Wait until the friend brings it up first
Send a text rather than say it out loud
Avoid the friend until time defuses it

cards.text: Point to the person in this room [Subject] is most likely to need to apologize to in the next year.
cards.playNotes: All point. Subject reveals who they think it's most likely to be. Scoring: 2 for pointing at the person Subject named. 3 to Subject if a majority pointed correctly.

cards.text: [Subject] is currently carrying an unresolved fight with a friend that's:

options.text: Less than a month old
Months old
Years old
[Subject] has no current unresolved fight

cards.text: The reason a past friendship of [Subject]'s ended was most likely:

options.text: Distance or life moving in different directions
A specific event that was never repaired
Slow drift, no specific cause
[Subject] outgrew the friendship
The friend outgrew [Subject]
Mutual realization that the friendship had run its course

cards.text: [Subject], tell us about a friendship that ended that you still think about. What would you say to that person if you could say it cleanly?
Group discussion: Is every friendship worth repairing? When is letting one go the right move, and how do you know?
When [Subject] has been wronged by a friend, [Subject]:

options.text: Says something within 24 hours
Sits with it for a few days then speaks
Lets it pile up until something breaks
Cuts the friend off without explaining

cards.text: If a stranger watched [Subject] for a month, they'd say [Subject] is:

options.text: Exactly the friend [Subject] claims to be
Better than [Subject] gives themselves credit for
Less of a friend than [Subject] thinks
A different kind of friend than [Subject] describes

cards.text: If [Subject]'s friends made a group chat without [Subject] in it (about [Subject], not against), the chat would mostly say:

options.text: [Subject] is the rock of the group
[Subject] is going through something and they're worried
[Subject] has been distant lately
[Subject] is doing great and they're proud

cards.text: The biggest gap between the friend [Subject] WANTS to be and the friend [Subject] ACTUALLY is, comes down to:

options.text: [Subject] talks more than they listen
[Subject] over-commits and under-delivers
[Subject] is consistent in flashes but not over time
[Subject] gives advice instead of presence
[Subject] disappears when life gets full
There is no significant gap

cards.text: [Subject] is the friend they wanted to be ten years ago.
The friend [Subject] would most like to BECOME more like is:

options.text: Someone in this room
An old friend [Subject] doesn't see often
A public figure [Subject] admires
Honestly, no one in particular

cards.text: If [Subject] could trade ONE habit with a friend in this room, [Subject] would trade their:

options.text: Communication habits
Conflict habits
Investment habits (time, energy)
Honesty habits

cards.text: Point to the person in this room whose friendship style [Subject] would most like to ADOPT.
cards.playNotes: All point. Subject reveals who they actually admire most. Scoring: 2 for pointing at the person Subject named. 3 to Subject if a majority pointed correctly.

cards.text: The friend version of [Subject] that does NOT exist yet, but that [Subject] wants to grow into, would mostly be characterized by:

options.text: Being slower to react and quicker to listen
Showing up before being asked
Saying the hard things sooner
Holding fewer friendships but holding them deeper
Holding more friendships and accepting they'll be lighter
Being okay being needed less

cards.text: [Subject], if you could rewrite one specific thing about how you've been a friend in the past year, what would it be?
Group discussion: If everyone in this room had to grade themselves as a friend, on a scale of one to ten, and announce the grade, what would you each give yourself and why?
cards.playNotes: Everyone weighs in. No scoring. The grading is for the conversation, not points.

cards.text: [Subject] thinks the people in this room would say [Subject] is best at:

options.text: Being there when it counts
Knowing what to say
Showing up consistently in small ways
Telling them the truth even when it's hard

cards.playNotes: Reveal. Subject reveals what they think. Others reveal what they actually believe. Scoring: 2 + 1.

cards.text: The version of [Subject] this game has shown to the room is:

options.text: Pretty close to who [Subject] thought they were
Better than [Subject] realized
Less than [Subject] wanted to be
Honestly, [Subject] has not made up their mind yet

cards.playNotes: This is the closer card. Subject reveals at the end of the night. Scoring: 2 + 1.
